Fuzzy clustering

Source: R/seg_cluster.R
seg_cluster_fuzzy.Rd

Assigns each respondent a membership degree for every cluster with fuzzy clustering (cluster::fanny()).

Usage

seg_cluster_fuzzy(
  x,
  k = 4,
  memb_exp = 1.1,
  max_iter = 1000,
  plots = TRUE,
  cluster_plot_args = list(),
  dend_args = list(),
  centers_args = list(),
  heatmap_n = 200,
  seed = 123,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

The output of seg_prep_data() (recommended), or a data frame or numeric matrix with already prepared clustering variables (no missing values).

k

Number of clusters. A vector (e.g. 2:6) returns one solution per number of clusters. Ignored by the density-based methods. For "mclust", NULL lets the BIC choose the number of clusters (slow).

memb_exp

Membership exponent (> 1). Defaults to 1.1, see "Details".

max_iter

Maximum number of iterations. Defaults to 1000.

plots

Logical. Whether to create the plots. Defaults to TRUE.

cluster_plot_args

A list of arguments passed to factoextra::fviz_cluster(), overriding the defaults (see seg_plot_cluster()), e.g. list(ellipse.type = "convex").

dend_args

A list of arguments passed to factoextra::fviz_dend(), overriding the defaults (see seg_plot_dend()), e.g. list(type = "phylogenic").

centers_args

A list of arguments passed to seg_plot_centers(), overriding the defaults, e.g. list(type = "bars", scale = "original").

heatmap_n

Number of respondents randomly sampled for the heatmap. Defaults to 200.

seed

Random seed. The global random seed is left untouched. Defaults to 123.

verbose

Logical. Whether to print the results. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

For a single number of clusters, an object of class seg_cluster, a list with the elements:

  • method, family: the clustering method and its family.

  • k: the requested number of clusters (NA for density-based methods).

  • k_found: the number of clusters found (excluding noise).

  • cluster: integer vector with the cluster of each respondent (0 = noise), in the order of the prepared data.

  • membership: matrix with the membership degrees (fuzzy) or probabilities (model-based) of each respondent in each cluster, NULL for the other methods.

  • sizes: tibble with the size and share of each cluster.

  • centers: tibble with the mean of each clustering variable per cluster.

  • assignment: tibble with the respondent identifier, the cluster and method-specific information (e.g. the highest membership degree).

  • data, data_full, dist: the prepared clustering variables, the original data of the retained respondents and the distance matrix (if available), as passed on from seg_prep_data().

  • fit: the result of the underlying clustering function.

  • tree: the hierarchical tree (class hclust) for hierarchical methods and hierarchical k-means, otherwise NULL.

  • cluster_map: named integer vector mapping the cluster codes of fit (names) to the renumbered codes, NULL if not renumbered.

  • prep: the preparation settings of seg_prep_data() (variables, missing values, rescaling parameters), used to prepare new respondents in predict.seg_cluster().

  • plots: list of plots (see "Visualizations").

  • settings: list of the settings used.

For several numbers of clusters, an object of class seg_cluster_set, a list with the elements solutions (named list of seg_cluster objects, e.g. solutions$k4), summary (tibble with the cluster sizes per solution), plot (the cluster plots of all solutions combined) and method.

Details

Algorithm

In "hard" clustering (e.g. k-means), each respondent belongs to exactly one cluster. In fuzzy clustering, each respondent \(i\) has a membership degree \(u_{ic}\) between 0 and 1 for each cluster \(c\), summing to 1. The algorithm minimizes $$\sum_{c=1}^{k} \frac{\sum_{i,j} u_{ic}^r u_{jc}^r d(i, j)}{2 \sum_j u_{jc}^r}$$ where \(d(i, j)\) is the distance between two respondents and \(r\) the membership exponent (memb_exp): respondents that are close to each other should have high memberships in the same clusters. Each respondent is assigned to the cluster with its highest membership degree (cluster); the membership degrees are returned in membership, and the highest membership degree of each respondent in assignment$membership_max.

Membership exponent

The membership exponent (\(r > 1\)) controls the fuzziness: the closer to 1, the crisper the solution; the larger, the fuzzier. The usual default of 2 leads to complete fuzziness (all memberships equal to 1/k) for survey data with many clustering variables, which is why the default here is 1.1. Dunn's partition coefficient (in settings$partition_coefficient) ranges from 1/k (completely fuzzy) to 1 (crisp); a warning is given if the solution is (almost) completely fuzzy.

When to use

When respondents are expected to belong partly to several segments, or to identify respondents that are clearly assigned (high membership) vs. respondents between segments (e.g. to exclude them when building a typing tool). The distance matrix of seg_prep_data() is used.

See also

Other clustering: predict.seg_cluster(), seg_agreement(), seg_as_cluster(), seg_cluster(), seg_cluster_density(), seg_cluster_hierarchical(), seg_cluster_hkmeans(), seg_cluster_model(), seg_cluster_partitioning(), seg_dbscan_eps(), seg_plot_centers(), seg_plot_cluster(), seg_plot_dend(), seg_plot_heatmap()

Examples

# \donttest{
prep <- seg_prep_data(
  sm_synthetic,
  vars = dplyr::starts_with("F50_0_"),
  missing = "mice",
  max_missing_prop = 0.2,
  verbose = FALSE
)
fz <- seg_cluster_fuzzy(prep, k = 4)
#> 
#> ── Cluster solution: Fuzzy clustering, k = 4 ──
#> 
#> • Cluster 1: n = 381 (28%)
#> • Cluster 2: n = 360 (26%)
#> • Cluster 3: n = 353 (26%)
#> • Cluster 4: n = 277 (20%)
#> Plots: `$plots$cluster`, `$plots$heatmap`, and `$plots$centers`
head(fz$membership)
#>    cluster_1   cluster_2 cluster_3   cluster_4

#> 2 0.53461197 0.143301176 0.3181298 0.003957007
#> 3 0.01380938 0.001488135 0.2815827 0.703119737
#> 4 0.05313373 0.039559339 0.8940031 0.013303829
#> 5 0.31711313 0.036899342 0.6407878 0.005199758
#> 6 0.03177246 0.006745253 0.8454946 0.115987657
# }
